graph.title: LEGO City 7936 Level Crossing (with wheeled railway excavator)

new_part_types.name: Plate 1x4 with clips (black, rail wheel holder)
Black axle bar with end pegs
Blue seat stand on 1x2 plate (booklet label 9566)

notes: Booklet has two numbered bags: bag 1 builds the wheeled railway excavator with a minifig worker; bag 2 builds the level crossing with two signals, two barriers and track. Both are built.

The excavator and the crossing are two separate models. The booklet's final pages (42-43) show the excavator standing on the crossing rails and page 41 shows it lifting the spare track. To keep one connected build, I added contact edges: rail wheel w1 rests on crossing track b63, and the hook b57 rests on the spare track b66. Those are not fastened joins.
Ids b21-b24 are intentionally skipped. The four tyre and rim pairs ('wheel' repeat) and the two rail-wheel units ('railwheel' repeat) are in repeats.
The excavator is built upside-down for the first steps. The stacking direction of plates in the first steps is inferred from the pictures.

Some inventory shapes are hard to identify from the thumbnails: 4181143 (large yellow brick, 2x6 or 2x8) and 4211002 (black plate, 2x6 or 2x8). The yellow brick is modelled in a single position at the back of the cab.
Stickers (7936 label, hazard stripes, red/white barrier stripes, X sign and arrows) are not modelled as parts.
The bucket 4140709 (step 17) is an alternative to the grab/hook, so b58 and b56/b57 both attach to the boom tip, in two separate pin holes.
The blue seat is labelled '9566' in the booklet's inventory. That is not a valid element ID and no element ID could be read from the page, so it is modelled as a new type 'lego-seat-stand-blue'.

Minifig uses catalogue generic types (head, hard hat, torso, legs) in place of Element IDs 4261301, 383321, 4275854, 4120158. The legs are joined to the seat with null ports, since the seat has no seat-port.

Inventory quantities not placed from the pictures: 241226 (5x listed, 2 used); 4535739 (4x listed, 2 used on the signals); 4540386 (2x listed, 1 used). The unplaced pieces are omitted rather than guessed.

Where a plate has many identical studs, new part types now have enough numbered studs for distinct ports. Catalogue plates have only one stud port, so extra joins to them, and the deck strips, ramps, sign tile and rim-to-tyre joins, use null ports. The exact stud position cannot be read from the pictures anyway.

The black axle bars b6/b7 sit over the studs of the grey hinge plates, so they are modelled with anti-stud ports. The signal pole is modelled with an anti-stud base so it fits into the round brick. The clip plate 4535739 joins to the underside (anti-stud) of the sign base plate; this position is inferred from page 34.

Black axle bar with end pegs

notes: Booklet has two numbered bags: bag 1 builds the wheeled railway excavator with a minifig worker; bag 2 builds the level crossing with two signals, two barriers and track. Both are built.
Ids b21-b24 are intentionally skipped. The four tyre and rim pairs (the 'wheel' repeat) and the two rail-wheel units ('railwheel' repeat) are in repeats.
The excavator is built upside-down for the first steps. Stacking direction of plates in the first steps (which side is up) is inferred from the pictures.

Some inventory shapes are hard to identify from the thumbnails: 4181143 (large yellow brick, 2x6 or 2x8) and 4211002 (black plate, 2x6 or 2x8). The yellow brick is modelled in a single position at the back of the cab.
Stickers (7936 label, hazard stripes, red/white barrier stripes, X sign and arrows) are not modelled as parts.
The bucket 4140709 (step 17) is an alternative to the grab/hook, so b58 and b56/b57 are both attached to the boom tip.

The 4 spare track pieces: the 4th track (b66) is the loose piece shown with the excavator on page 41, so it has no joins. The two connecting pins removed in the step 1 note on page 25 are discarded and not modelled.
Minifig uses catalogue generic types (head, hard hat, torso, legs) in place of Element IDs 4261301, 383321, 4275854, 4120158.

Inventory quantities that could not be placed from the pictures: 241226 (5x listed, only 2 shown as used); 4535739 (4x listed, 2 used on the signals); 4210636 (3x listed, 3 used); 4540386 (2x listed, 1 used); 4211111 (2x, used in the gate bases). Those unplaced pieces are omitted rather than guessed.

The exact studs a piece sits on cannot be seen in the pictures, so ports are the first stud/anti-stud of each part (e.g. stud.1). The deck strips and ramps are attached to the crossing track b63 without sub-position.
